one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window. (1) Cadence Q3 2026 results, most likely Oct 26 after the close. This is an aggregator estimate: as of Oct 1 Cadence has not issued its webcast notice (the Q2 notice came three weeks ahead), so a small chance remains that it lands just outside the window. The Q3 guide is $1.595-1.625B and $2.01-2.07 EPS, with consensus near the midpoint ($1.61B / $2.04). With an $8.1B backlog and a Q2 that raised FY26 EPS by $0.20, a modest beat is likely. The swing factor is any early FY2027 color against roughly 13% consensus growth. Cadence guides conservatively: FY26 started at $8.05-8.15 ex-Hexagon, so a cautious tone would be in character. (2) The Oct 28 FOMC: Polymarket has 26% hike odds on $21.4M volume. The September 19% drawdown came with rising yields and no company news, so a hike surprise is a real downside risk for the multiple. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways. A beat would be rewarded on the day (Synopsys rose 13.4% the day after its August beat), but that did not protect it from the later rate-driven selloff (-21% by Sep 15). Against that, CDNS is up 28% in 12 sessions, including a sympathy +6% on Oct 1 after Synopsys's investor day, which raises giveback risk. Net: median about $350 (spot) and lognormal sigma 0.13, slightly above annual vol / 3.5 (11.7%) to cover the earnings gap and FOMC risk. Unchanged from round 1; the supervisor found no directional edge either.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 of about $10.63 (0.25 x FY27 consensus $9.56 + 0.75 x FY28 est. $10.99) x 34x = $361. 40% forward FCF yield: NTM FCF of about $2.37B at 2.4% = $98.8B EV, less about $0.6B horizon net debt, over 276M diluted shares = $356. Blended about $359.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at 2027-10-01 of $10.63 x 34x

inputs_detail.derivation: Guide path: Feb $8.05-8.15 ex-Hexagon, cut in Q1 to $7.85-7.95 to include Hexagon, raised in Q2 back to $8.05-8.15. Organic beats recovered the Hexagon dilution within the year.
StockAnalysis $9.56 (26 analysts); Zacks about $9.43-9.54. This is one sell-side consensus, not independent confirmations.

FY27 $9.56 x 1.15. That is about 13% revenue growth (the consensus 2027 pace; SemiAnalysis's 13% EDA CAGR; Synopsys's 15% long-term model as the peer ceiling), plus modest operating leverage, plus about 1% net buyback accretion. No agentic revenue is assumed, because Cadence has disclosed none.

Today CDNS trades at about 36.7x FY27 consensus ($350.73 / $9.56). Synopsys, after a 13% jump to $490.54 on Oct 1, trades at about 25.7x its own FY27 guide ($19.08 midpoint) with 15% guided growth, against about 13% for Cadence. The Sep-15 low was about 30x NTM, and a 5.29% 10-year caps multiple expansion. I trim 35x to 34x: a persistent premium for Cadence's analog/hardware franchise and backlog visibility, but less than today's roughly 43% premium to Synopsys, plus a residual AI-disruption discount.

Grown about 15% a year, in line with the consensus EPS path (FY27 EPS +17.5%, revenue +13%).

$2.5B debt less $1.44B cash at Q2 2026. Over five quarters, retained FCF after buybacks of about $200M a quarter is about $1.4B, but some of it goes to tuck-ins and working capital. I assume net debt falls about $0.45B, consistent with the supervisor's $0.5-1.0B horizon range.
FY26 diluted share guide of 275.5-277.5M (Q2 CFO commentary). Corrected from 274M: buybacks at about $200M a quarter roughly offset dilution from equity comp, not reduce the count.
The current price implies about 2.2% on FY27 FCF; the Sep-15 low implied about 2.8%. 2.4% sits between them: no re-rating, a modest AI-disruption discount, and a 10-year at 5.29%.

bear.story: The AI-disruption narrative hardens. Another Kimi-style open-source or agentic demo moves toward advanced nodes, funded startups (ChipAgents $134M, Cognichip) win verification budget, or seat growth visibly slows. A conservative Feb-2027 FY27 guide (Cadence's habit, as the FY26 guide path showed) lands below about 13% growth, and yields stay above 5%. The China Affiliates Rule suspension lapses on Jan 10, 2027, putting part of the 15% China revenue at risk. NTM EPS falls to about $9.6 and the multiple compresses to about 26x, around Synopsys's level and below the Sep-15 trough of about 30x.

base.story: FY2027 plays out near consensus (about 13% revenue growth, $9.56 EPS), with organic beats offsetting the conservative initial guide as in 2026. Agent revenue is small but appears in commentary. Backlog stays above $8B, and the multiple settles at 34-35x on NTM EPS of about $10.63, still at a premium to Synopsys.

bull.story: Agentic products (ChipStack, ViraStack, AgentStack) turn into priced revenue visible in FY2027 guidance, on the model Devgan described: per-agent pricing at roughly one engineer's work, layered on top of base licenses whose numbers are 'already increasing somewhat'. Synopsys's 15% long-term model and its FY27 +15% guide show the industry demand is real, the 2027 hyperscaler capex build keeps design starts high, and the stock re-rates to about 43x on NTM EPS of about $11.2.

thesis_break_reason: Sentiment and yields alone took CDNS to $273.96 on Sep 15, 2026 with no company news, and the 52-week low is $262.75, so the $260s-270s are within proven noise. $245 is about 7% below that low and about 23x NTM EPS at the horizon, under Synopsys's roughly 25.7x FY27. Trading there would most likely mean real fundamental damage: an FY2027 guide well below about 13% growth even allowing for Cadence's conservative guiding, backlog falling from $8.1B, visible agent-driven seat or price compression at leading-edge nodes, or China access lost when the Affiliates Rule suspension ends on Jan 10, 2027.

reasoning: Round-2 revision after the supervisor's review, with 6 follow-up searches and fetches plus one Twelve Data pull. What changed: (1) Diluted shares corrected to 276M (FY26 guide 275.5-277.5M). (2) I took on the supervisor's verified context: the FY26 EPS guide path (Feb ex-Hexagon, Q1 cut, Q2 raised back), which shows Cadence guides conservatively and organic beats absorb dilution; the 10-year at 5.29%; Polymarket's 26% Oct-FOMC hike odds; the Affiliates Rule suspension to Jan 10, 2027; and an unconfirmed Q3 date. (3) Per source_review I rebased the agent-pricing bull case on Devgan's own words (More Than Moore Q&A, refetched: per-agent pricing at roughly one human's work, consumption pricing for new work, license numbers 'already increasing somewhat') and dropped Tech Fund's $25-50k per agent from any number. (4) I verified Synopsys's investor-day FY27 guide ($11.1-11.2B, $19.04-19.12 non-GAAP EPS, 15% CAGR to 2030) and its $490.54 close on Oct 1, which puts SNPS at about 25.7x FY27 against CDNS at about 36.7x. With Synopsys guiding faster growth and a 5.29% 10-year, I trim my target P/E from 35x to 34x. A Sep-23 Deutsche Bank conference takeaway (Semicon Alpha) repeats management's 'AI is a tailwind' line but adds no numbers. (5) Hiring alt-data conflicts across trackers (550-919 open roles), so I give it no weight. Fair value moves from $365 to $359: P/E $361 (10.63 x 34x) at 60%, FCF yield $356 (2.4% on NTM $2.37B, net debt about $0.6B, 276M shares) at 40%. The share-count correction cuts the FCF leg by about $3, while lower horizon net debt adds about $2. Scenarios are $250 / $365 / $480 at 25/50/25 (mean about $365). The ladder is a 92/8 mixture: a lognormal with median $359 and sigma 0.34, plus a disruption-tail lognormal with median $250 and sigma 0.40, kept per the supervisor's note and tied to the two 9-10% headline drops in 2026. The overall median is about $351 (spot) and P(>=351) = 0.50. I agree with the supervisor's $245 thesis break and its fair value (about $358). My view differs slightly on the multiple: I see the Synopsys gap as a reason to stay at or below 34x rather than a supporting comparison. The 1-month ladder is unchanged (median $350, sigma 0.13).
